(a) Report.—Not later than 120 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of Veterans Affairs shall submit to the Committee on Veterans’ Affairs of the Senate and the Committee on Veterans’ Affairs of the House of Representatives a report that details the plans of the Secretary to reduce the inventory of work items listed in the Monday Morning Workload Report under End Products 130, 137, 173, 290, 400, 600, 607, 690, 930, and 960. 
    (b) Sense of Congress.—It is the sense of Congress that the Secretary of Veterans Affairs should include in each Monday Morning Workload Report published by the Secretary the following:
        (1) With respect to each regional office of the Department of Veterans Affairs, the following:
            (A) The number of fully developed claims for benefits under the laws administered by the Secretary that have been received. 
            (B) The number of claims described in subparagraph (A) that are pending a decision. 
            (C) The number of claims described in subparagraph (A) that have been pending a decision for more than 125 days.  
        (2) Enhanced information on appeals of decisions relating to claims for benefits under the laws administered by the Secretary that are pending, including information contained in the reports of the Department entitled “Appeals Pending” and “Appeals Workload By Station”.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that the reporting requirement and the reference to "published" workload reports and "appeals" signal procedural engagement with outsiders. But the report goes only to congressional committees, which are inside the federal government, and the sense-of-Congress provision merely lists data the VA should include in its own workload report. No outside party is consulted, given a hearing or comment opportunity, or granted a right to sue over a federal decision.
fable.s: the Secretary of Veterans Affairs shall submit to the Committee on Veterans’ Affairs of the Senate and the Committee on Veterans’ Affairs of the House of Representatives a report

qwen_block.w: The section requires the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to submit a report to congressional committees. Congress is part of the federal government, so this interaction is internal to the government and does not involve outside parties. The 'Sense of Congress' provision merely expresses a preference for internal reporting metrics and does not mandate public participation or consultation with non-federal entities.
qwen_block.s: the Secretary of Veterans Affairs shall submit to the Committee on Veterans’ Affairs of the Senate and the Committee on Veterans’ Affairs of the House of Representatives a report

opus.w: The only formal interaction is a report to congressional committees, and Congress is inside the federal government. The sense-of-Congress part only suggests what data the Secretary should publish in a workload report. That is one-way disclosure, not consulting outsiders before a decision. The mention of appeals describes statistics to report and does not grant anyone a right to appeal or object.
opus.s: the Secretary of Veterans Affairs shall submit to the Committee on Veterans’ Affairs of the Senate and the Committee on Veterans’ Affairs of the House of Representatives a report that details the plans of the Secretary to reduce the inventory of work items
opus.b: The tempting reading is that this section is procedural: it requires a formal report and asks the VA to publish workload data, including data on appeals. Neither part brings in anyone from outside the federal government. The report goes to congressional committees, which are inside the government. The publication suggestion only shares information one way, and the reference to "appeals" just describes the data to be published. It does not give anyone a right to appeal or object.

qwen_chat.w: This section requires the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to submit a report to congressional committees. Congress is part of the federal government, so reporting to it is an intra-governmental action, not participation with outside parties. The content of the report concerns internal workload metrics and plans for processing claims, which falls under the exclusion for applications for benefits or internal administrative processes.
qwen_chat.s: Not later than 120 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of Veterans Affairs shall submit to the Committee on Veterans’ Affairs of the Senate and the Committee on Veterans’ Affairs of the House of Representatives a report that details the plans of the Secretary to reduce the inventory of work items listed in the Monday Morning Workload Report
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the report details plans to reduce inventory of work items (claims), it involves public participation in the decision-making process regarding veterans' benefits. However, the definition explicitly excludes applications for benefits or grants, and reporting on internal workload metrics to Congress is an internal government action. Congress is inside the federal government, so reporting to it is not participation with outside parties.
